title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Connection Reuse and Resumption Tickets Architecture
purpose: Define DoQ client and server policies for connection reuse, single-use resumption tickets, connectivity-change detection, address validation token gating, resumption ticket lifetime, and anti-replay mechanisms.
design_summary: Policy-layer additions: (1) DoqClient uses IdleTimeoutMargin with the advertised QUIC idle timeout to avoid reusing a connection too close to close time. (2) DoqClient tracks ticket usage via IsTicketUsed and rejects second use. (3) DoqClient stores PriorConnectivityId and ConnectivityId; a mismatch causes QueryAsync to throw so callers open fresh connections. (4) DoqClient.UseAddressValidationWithResumptionOnly defaults to true. (5) DoqServerOptions adds ResumptionTicketLifetime (default 6 hours) and EnableAntiReplay (default true). REQ-0103 (edns-tcp-keepalive prohibition) is cross-referenced to slice 0008. The transport layer does not expose local addresses or ticket internals; the client properties are policy knobs the caller populates.
data_and_state_considerations: The client adds a ticket-used boolean, two connectivity identity strings, and an address-validation policy flag. The server adds two configuration properties.
edge_cases_and_constraints: ConnectivityId is caller-managed; the client cannot detect network changes independently.
Ticket single-use tracking is per-instance; a new DoqClient is required for each ticket.
ResumptionTicketLifetime is an advisory server-side option; actual ticket lifetime depends on the TLS layer.
EnableAntiReplay is a policy toggle; the transport layer must implement the actual mechanism.
risks: The transport layer's session ticket store and TLS anti-replay state are not directly accessible from the DoQ adapter.

supplemental_sections.heading: Transport Abstraction
supplemental_sections.content: Resumption ticket single-use and connectivity-change detection are enforced at the DoQ adapter policy layer. Transport-level enforcement (tls ticket store, local address tracking) is managed by the caller or future transport extensions.
